Now after inter-globe aviation hiked their fuel surcharge on domestic and international flights,
summit searching ATF prices, India's aviation minister Kijarapuramon Nairu has delayed
concerns, saying that the ministry will take stock off the impact with the oil marketing companies
and the airlines.
One of the most important things is the West Asia crisis and how it is putting a big burden
on the ATF prices.
But we are still in discussion, both with the airlines and also the OAMCs.
Let us see how the discussion unfolds.
Now additionally, the aviation minister has also assured that the ministry will meet airlines
and the Mumbai International Airport to resolve the dispute over the proposed changes to flight
operations ahead of the closure and the redevelopment of the terminal one.
We will let the meeting happen.
The ministry is going to have a meeting with the stakeholders and once we understand the
point of view from all the stakeholders, then we will take a decision.
And staying with this subject, Madhya is now joining in to tell us what is the likely agenda
going to be for this big meeting.
Well, the big question going into this meeting is whether the government can get the airport
operator and airlines on the same page.
That is very important because they have been, you know, there has been a standoff between
the two sides.
The meeting is likely to start at 2 p.m. just a short while from now, officials from Mumbai
Airport, Navi Mumbai Airport, airlines and airline bodies IATA and FIA are expected to be present
in this meeting.
And airlines are expected to seek a detailed roadmap for the refurbishment of terminal one
of Mumbai Airport, what exactly is being demolished or refurbished, the different phases and the timelines
for each phase.
The second big issue is capacity airlines want clarity on the actual capacity and utilization
of both terminal one and terminal two.
And importantly, how much additional capacity will be created after the refurbishment of terminal
one because that feeds directly into the third issue, the transition plan.
Mumbai Airport remember has proposed temporarily discontinuing 265 weekly international departure
slots from T2 from October 25 and airlines had time till today to give a list of these
flights that they will cancel.
Now, airlines are likely to seek clarity on the methodology behind this number, how the
traffic movement is expected to work and what operational impact will be on their networks
and airlines are likely to question if the airport operator can actually cancel flights that
are approved in the winter schedule as per which airlines have planned their network and their
flights.
And the fourth, the perhaps the most important issue is consultation airlines are expected to
push for any transition plan to be discussed, transparently with all stakeholders in a grid
collectively before implementation.
Other big issue also on the table is Navi Mumbai's preparedness to handle the proposed transition
from Mumbai T2 airlines are expected to seek a detailed readiness assessment across critical
operational areas, not just passenger infrastructure.
That includes aircraft engineering and line maintenance, whether certified maintenance providers
are available at this airport for each aircraft type and whether the required DGC approvals
are in place.
So, capacity assessment, redevelopment plan, basis for reduction of 265 flights at T2 and
Navi Mumbai airports preparedness to handle these additional flights.
That is likely to be the crux of today's meeting that is expected to start at 2pm.
Madhya, thank you for that update.
Then, our shifting focus to the Tata group.
Tata Trust is venue for innovation and which I think had written to the SDTT alleging that
they had not been consulted over the proposal to merge companies into the trusts on the 30th
of September.
Four trustees from the Sir Dharajee Tata Trusts namely Noel Tata, Dharaya Kambata, Bhaskar
Bhatt and Neville Tata have replied to the letter rebutting these allegations.
The response state that innovation and sing breached fiduciary duties and undermined the
trust stand on the listing of Tata Sons and that the pair backed the listing publicly
from April of this year, but did not raise it at three SDTT meetings since then.
Now the response also defends the letter written on the 28th of September advocating to keep
Tata Sons private.
The trustees also claim that Srinivasan and sing indulged in contradictory conduct as they
sought the charity commissioner's intervention to prevent the SDTT from acting while also
asking for decisions to be made collectively.
The issue will now be taken forward with the charity commissioner who has given the Sir Dharajee
Tata Trusts a seven day deadline to reply to the letter written by Vainus Renevasan and Vijay
Singh.
Of course, the big trigger tomorrow is the RBI monetary policy and the consensus is that the
RBI may raise rates by 25 basis points.
Ritu is here with the findings from the CNBC TV 18 poll and the key expectations from the
policy.
While the RBI's rate setting panel is set to announce its policy decision and R poll
leaves little doubt on the expected action, all of our respondents that's 100% expect RBI
to raise their reparate by 25 basis points to 5.5%, and this would be the first hike after
four consecutive holes at 5.25%.
Now what's changed in a month?
Crude above $100, August CPI at a 22-month high, the Fed and the ECB have already high grades
and the rupee is hovering around 96.
So the case for acting has fendant pretty quickly.
On the stance, 60% of our respondents expect MPC to stay on neutral.
Another 30% expected move to withdrawal of accommodation, while 10% expect RBI to keep
the stance but tweak the wording to signal more tightening.
As for how steep this entire hike cycle will be, 60% expect a total of 50 basis points
of heights, 30% expect 75 and 10% expect a full 100 basis points.
The expectation is we will see the second hike coming as early as December.
On growth the respondents are pretty evenly split, one half expects the number to be revised
up to 6.8% to 7% and the other half between 7% to 7.2% on inflation, 80% expect RBI to raise
the forecast from 5% to anywhere between 5.1% to 5.4% with the higher oil prices that
are around in Maharashtra all of that adding to the risk.
Now liquidity is another key piece because RBI has already begun raining the surplus ahead
of this rate hike through VEE Triple R which is radiable rate reverse repot and open market
operations from here on.
Half our respondents expect more VEE Triple R's, 30% see no new measures, 10% see more OMO sales
and another 10% expect even a CRR hike.
Now on the governor's commentary 70% are expecting a very cautious data dependent tone and 30%
aboard Hockishwan and finally when asked what they will watch out for most closely our respondents
pointed to the policy tone, the inflation outlook, the length of the rate hike cycle, further
liquidity absorption measures and any macro-prudential curves to slow down lending in specific segments.
Rhythm, thank you for setting us up with the expectations from tomorrow's RBI policy.
Take a short break, back with more on the other side.
Back now as regulators keep a watch on tariffs.
If there is a necessity, we will intervene.
That's the word coming in from the telecom regulatory authority chairman Anil Kumar Lahati.
The regulator said that the TRII will play the required role in the future.
On research reports flagging tariff hikes, the chairman said that the TRII will not act based on
guesswork, listen in the slice of that conversation.
As far as tariff is concerned, as per the present regulatory provisions, the tariff is under
forbearance which means the tariff is to be decided by the operators.
There was a time point of time when the tariff was decided by TRII or it required approval of the TRII.
But since then there is already competition in the sector and the tariff is prevailing in the
country are probably the lowest in the world which is a confirmation of the competition prevailing
in the country.
So the market forces are taking care of the tariff already.
So as regulators we do keep a watch on the tariffs and as soon as there is a necessity of
intervention we will do that.
But you do not feel any necessity of any intervention even if there were to be another 10 to 15%
hike as and when it were to come through.
I do not think we can act on this based on guesswork.
There are crores of subscribers who use feature points and do not consume data.
Also there are several elderly persons, senior citizens who are not comfortable using data
and we receive a number of representations from such subscribers or consumer advocacy groups
and other forums that they want to have a plan without data but they do not have that choice.
So it is in this context that TRII has mandated that the service provider should also provide
choice of plans without the data.
Now, the Roshuga prices have hit an 18 one high and are up 33% this year as tightening
global supplies meet aggressive regulatory moves in India. Manisha is here with more details on this.
Well the surge in sugar prices are just about continued. We have seen prices gain up by nearly
10% in the last one week itself and it has been a 14% of a jump in the last one month.
If you look at the overnight markets it has been a 4% of again in the Roshuga futures
and in this year till time well it has been a strong 33% of gain in the sweetener there in.
Well, various reasons for that and I will start with the Indian markets first. We are on first of
October India was holding a stock of 36 Lakh tons. Now the expectation is that during the festival
season you could be looking at 25 to 26 Lakh tons of demand coming in for this month there in.
The aggressive regulatory intervention that Indian government has made in sense of sugar whether
it has been about stock limits or stock reporting etc has led to a correction in case of prices
there in. But the expectation is that the government could perhaps completely halt any diversion from
the sugar into ethanol this year or this season around. Also the dealer stock limit well that has
been reduced to 2000 quintals between October 15 to November 30th. What the street will watch out for
also is the early crushing this time around. Usually crushing starts at Diwali after Diwali but because
there is a concern about sugar stocks right now we could be looking at sugar crushing starting from
third week of October. Now that will bring recoveries down by 1 to 1 and a half percent but the street
believes that this is something that many mills perhaps in UP Maharashtra could be looking at as well.
The imports is something that India perhaps is not any more feasible one Lakh tons had been
around to be imported until 31st of October but with the global sugar prices gaining by 10% in
last one month itself this is a number that perhaps will not be completed but the major concerns
clearly are from the international markets where we are looking at a deficit in this season and there
is lower crop also from other areas. Brazil which is the largest producer of sugar is looking at heavy
rains and delay in harvest. European Union is looking at 19% of a decline in sugar production.
Thailand production is expected to see a decline by 17% as well. So all of these factors perhaps would
be very supportive for sugar prices going forward and India next season as well as looking at some
concerns because of El Nino so John not this this season but the next season as well in focus right now.
